title: Dependability Radar — Commitment Ledger & Pulse Plan
content:
Purpose:
This is a working ledger for the cross-functional dependability program. Goal is to move from a static SLO catalog to a living 'Dependability Radar' that captures service maturity bands, risk-weighted commitments, and a 30/60 pulse experiment plan we can run with product, infra, and SRE partners.

Context / why this is different:
- Many teams have SLOs documented but few maintain a prioritized, up-to-date list of pragmatic commitments tied to customer impact and operational cost.
- Instead of a single top-down SLO rollout, this ledger pairs a compact radar view (maturity + risk + signal confidence) with a short experiment cadence to converge on realistic SLOs and remediation paths.
- Emphasis on cross-team tradeoffs — product owners own customer impact buckets, SRE owns signal & alerting hygiene, infra owns capacity/backfill.

High-level proposal:
1) Dependability Radar (monthly): a 1-page table for each service with columns: maturity band (green/amber/red), primary customer impact, recommended commitment (latency/availability target), signal confidence (high/med/low), remediation runbook link, risk score (1-10).
2) Commitment Ledger (ongoing): an append-only ledger where each change to a commitment includes rationale, author, stakeholders, linked experiment ID, and rollback criteria.
3) Pulse experiments (30/60 day cycles): small, measurable experiments to validate commitments and observability gaps. Example pulses: simulated load spike for a latency-sensitive route, KV-cache warmup test, prefix cache effectiveness test, alert deduplication window reduction.

Success criteria (how we know this helped):
- Within 90 days, 60% of services in the radar have an actionable commitment with signal confidence >= med and an assigned owner for remediation.
- Mean time to detect (MTTD) for critical degradation reduces by 25% for services in the green/amber bands after 2 pulses.
- Number of on-call interruptions caused by known noisy alerts drops by 30% across participating services.

Roles & Responsibilities:
- Program lead: Ava Chen (coordination, radar cadence, ledger governance)
- SRE liaison: Priya Raman (signal/alert hygiene, runbook alignment)
- Product partner(s): Omar Castillo (customer impact prior), Sofia Martinez (release gating for high-impact changes)
- Infra lead: Liam Nguyen (capacity, fallbacks, dedicated pool plans)
- Service owners: assigned per-service (TBD in first radar run)

Pulse experiment template (we will store experiment artifacts in the linked experiments board):
- Experiment ID: EX-2026-01-01
- Hypothesis: If we reduce alert dedup window from 10m to 3m for route X, noisy alerts reduce and MTTD improves without increasing false positives > 5%.
- Measurement: alert count / week, false positive ratio, time to acknowledge, customer error rate for route X.
- Success gates: false positive ratio <= 5%, ack time improves by 15%
- Rollback criteria: false positives > 8% or any customer-visible error increase > 0.5%

Initial 90-day plan (draft dates):
- Week 0-2: Radar kick — collect service inventories (focus: top 25 services by traffic + top 10 by customer impact). Quick intake template will be emailed.
- Week 3-4: First radar snapshot, triage meeting (cross-functional), assign owners + pick first 8 pulses.
- Day 30: Pulse review #1 (synthesis of findings, dashboard updates, ledger entries created).
- Day 60: Pulse review #2 (adjust commitments, expand signal coverage).
- Day 90: Consolidated commit window — move validated commitments to the 'operational catalog' and schedule remaining remediation work into teams' roadmaps.

Minimum tooling & data we need:
- Per-route latency and error histograms (P50/P90/P99) in a central dashboard.
- Deployment / rollout metadata attached to commit IDs (link to GitHub/PRs).
- Alert taxonomy and noise metrics (who, when, why) surfaced in a shared dashboard.
- A simple ledger page (Confluence/Drive table) where entries are timestamped and searchable.

Communication cadence:
- Weekly 30m sync for program core team (Ava, Priya, Omar, Liam) — status, blockers, experiment escalations.
- Bi-weekly 60m cross-functional radar review with service owners and PMs.
- Slack channel: #dependability-radar (for live notes, quick calls-to-action).

Risk log (quick sketches):
- Risk: Teams treat ledger as another doc to ignore. Mitigation: tie commitments to release gating signals and include commitments in postmortems.
- Risk: Over-optimizing for SLO numbers increases infra cost. Mitigation: every commitment has cost estimate and a business owner sign-off.
- Risk: Observability blind spots lead to overconfident commitments. Mitigation: require 'signal confidence' >= med to publish green-band commitments.

Open questions (for the triage meeting):
- What exact threshold defines the maturity bands? (suggestion: green: no recent incidents + high signal confidence; amber: recent recoveries needed; red: frequent customer impact)
- Which topologies are excluded initially (e.g., experimental model-serving endpoints vs public API)?
- How do we index service membership for multi-tenant infra (who owns the SLO?)

Immediate next actions (owner):
- Ava: publish intake template and spreadsheet by 2026-01-15; set calendar invites for Week 3 triage.
- Priya: compile current alert noise dashboard and export noisy-alert top-20 by volume by 2026-01-18.
- Omar: pull customer-impact mappings for top product flows by 2026-01-18.
- Liam: validate capacity headroom for dedicated pool experiments; flag services that cannot run stress tests by 2026-01-20.

Notes to self / rough drafting comments:
- Keep ledger entries short, timestamped, and linked to experiments. Avoid long prose — prefer bullets.
- We will iterate the radar visualization (heatmap vs table) — start with a simple table and iterate.
- Emphasize that a 'commitment' is a pragmatic operating target, not a legal SLA.

Appendix: intake template fields (short):
- Service name
- Owner(s)
- Primary customer impact category (data loss, latency, correctness, availability)
- Current measurement endpoints (dashboard links)
- Current maturity band (green/amber/red)
- Suggested commitment (metric + target)
- Signal confidence (H/M/L)
- First pulse idea
- Estimated effort (S/M/L)

End of draft ledger entry. Please add comments inline or in the Slack thread.

Decision log: (live)
- 2026-01-12: created by Ava — initial proposal to run 30/60 pulses and maintain a ledger.
- 2026-01-20: agreed to focus intake on 35 services for initial radar (top traffic + product impact).

---
This is a working doc; expect choppy notes, TODOs and questions. The aim is to produce a practical, low-overhead mechanism to make commitments visible, testable, and owned across product, infra, and SRE.
